failures.reason: The loaded well entity now has one static identity frame. DrawingWell owns the runtime pail/mechanism/water composite, so expecting six frames on the static entity is stale. Direct native runtime sampling additionally exposes an existing covered idle-water glint defect, described below; this PR does not weaken the visible-motion requirement or change that runtime.

native_idle_water_comparison.method: Instantiate unmodified Game(fullscreen=False,start_on_title=False), set town.reduced_motion=False, sample snapshot(town.well.sprite(t)) for t=0,200,400,600,800,1000. Hash complete native RGBA surface bytes. No sprite/renderer mock and no runtime edits.
native_idle_water_comparison.finding: Both revisions produce one unique native idle composite across six ambient phases. DrawingWell writes phase glints at logical (29+phase,69) and (48-phase,69) before compositing front_rim. The native rim is opaque over these locations and covers the glints. This is not proof of visible well-water animation.
native_idle_water_comparison.followup: In a separate well presentation PR, establish visible shaft-water pixels in the authored native structure/front-rim registration and composite the ambient phases at that visible surface. Preserve the fixed roof/rope/crank and one-pail ownership/handoff rules; replace stale tests with production native phase, mask/alpha, reduced-motion and actual actor-depth checks without removing the visible-motion assertion.

scope_decision: Keep tests/test_well.py exactly as at the baseline commit. No expectedFailure markers, skips, assertion weakening or well-runtime/art changes are included. Report the 79/81 civic result separately from the passing core and story suites; retain the original intended water-motion requirement for the scoped follow-up.
